  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
  methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
  Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
  meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
  comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

  Watch the Meeting Online

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 20, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code §53646, the
  Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2022-2023 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for May 2023.

  D. APPROVAL OF A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT FOR THE
  ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF
  THE COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING PROGRAM AND
  WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE UPPER LOS ANGELES RIVER
  WATERSHED MANAGEMENT AREA IN THE AMOUNT OF $13,688 FOR THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24

  Staff recommends the approval of a Memorandum of Agreement (MOU)
  between the City of San Gabriel, along with 18 other governmental agencies
  and the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments for administration and cost
  sharing among the agencies related to the implementation of the Coordinated
  Integrated Program and Watershed Management Plan for the Upper Los
  Angeles River Watershed Management Area. The proposed budget for Fiscal
  Year 2023-24 includes funding for the first year of this MOU. However, due to
  monitoring and reporting requirements to meet compliance schedules, the
  costs vary during the length of the three-year term. As such, funding for future
  fiscal years will be planned and budgeted accordingly.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the Memorandum of Agreement for the Administration and Cost Sharing for
  the Implementation of the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program and
  Watershed Management Area and approve a purchase order in an amount not
  to exceed $13,688 from account number 138-800-03-22-000.

  E. INTER-CON CONTRACT EXTENSION IN THE AMOUNT OF $137,932 FOR
  PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2023

  The Professional Services Agreement with Inter-Con Security Systems Inc.
  contract to provide parking enforcement services expires on June 30, 2023. Staff
  recommends the extension of the contract for an additional six months, ending
  December 31, 2023, to engage further research into alternative parking-
  enforcement services. The cost for the six-month extension is $137,932. Parking
  enforcement services are currently budgeted in the amount of $276,000 for
  Fiscal Year 2022-23. $350,000 was budgeted for parking enforcement services
  for Fiscal Year 2023-24 due to forecasted cost escalations.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to extend
  the current contract with Inter-Con for an additional six months, ending on
  December 31, 2023. Staff will re-evaluate their services and/or seek other
  opportunities for services for the remainder of Fiscal Year 2023-24.

  F. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JOHN L. HUNTER AND
  ASSOCIATES, INCORPORATED IN THE AMOUNT OF $46,900 TO PROVIDE
  NATIONAL POLLUTANT DISCHARGE ELIMINATION SYSTEM PROGRAM
  MANAGEMENT SUPPORT SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24

  Staff seeks to award a Professional Services Agreement with John L. Hunter and
  Associates, Inc. to provide National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System
  Program Management Support Services and approve purchase orders in the
  amount not to exceed $46,900 for Fiscal Year 2023-24 and $7,035 in an
  additional contingency amount. Funding for the first year of this Professional

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  4
   Services Agreement is included in the Stormwater (Measure W) account.
  However, due to Consumer Price Index annual increases, the costs will vary
  during the length of the agreement. As such, funding for future fiscal years will
  be planned and budgeted accordingly.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Professional Service Agreement with John L. Hunter and Associates, Inc. and
  approve purchase orders in the amount not to exceed $46,900 and a
  contingency amount of $7,035 from the Stormwater (Measure W) account 138-
  800-03-22-000 for Fiscal Year 2023-24.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 23-41 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 300 BLOCK OF BRIDGE STREET

  Request for a temporary street closure to host a block party on Sunday, July 2,
  2023, on the 300 block of Bridge Street between Sycamore Drive to the end of
  the cul-de-sac. There is no fiscal impact related to this item. Normally scheduled
  staff time will be used for this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-41 authorizing
  closure on Bridge Street between Sycamore Drive to the end of the cul-de-sac
  from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Sunday, July 2, 2023.

  H. RESOLUTION NO. 23-37: COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM PARTICIPATING CITY-
  COOPERATION AGREEMENT

  The City receives Community Development Block Grant funds administered
  through the Los Angeles County Development Agency. Every three years, the
  County must re-qualify for the Urban County designation and entitlement
  status from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, which
  allows the Los Angeles County Development Agency to administer Community
  Development Block Grant funds directly to the City. For the City to continue

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  5
   participating and receive funding directly from the Los Angeles County
  Development Agency, the City must execute a Cooperation Agreement with the
  County and adopt the proposed Resolution. The City of San Gabriel’s
  Community Development Block Grant funding allocation estimate for Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 is $300,561.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-37 authorizing the City’s participation in the Los
  Angeles Urban County Community Development Block Grant Program; and

  2. Authorize the Mayor or their designee to execute all documents necessary
  for participation in the Los Angeles Urban County Community Development
  Block Grant Program on behalf of the City of San Gabriel.

  I. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 23-42, RELATED TO PERMANENT LOCAL
  HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) YEAR 3 FUNDING AND PROPOSED
  ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, will be applying for funding for Year
  3 of the Permanent Local Housing Allocation Program from the California
  Department of Housing & Community Development. The allocation is based
  on real estate recording fees, and it is estimated that the City of San Gabriel will
  be allocated $334,526 from the $18 million grant for the period July 1, 2023 –
  June 2024 (Year 3). The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to utilize this
  funding for the eligible housing activities as identified in the PLHA grant
  guidelines. Staff is recommending adoption of the Resolution by the City
  Council and allocation of the $334,526 to assist the City in developing its first
  potential affordable housing project at 405 S. Del Mar Ave, which is an eligible
  activity under the grant guidelines. If the State approves the eligible activities,
  the City is expected to have access to the $334,526 reimbursable grant through
  LACDA by July 1, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  6
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-42 which
  approves the following actions:

  1. Elect the following eligible activities, subject to the State approval, for Year
  3 of the 5-year Permanent Local Housing Allocation grant period:
  (1) The predevelopment, development, acquisition, rehabilitation,
  and preservation of multifamily, residential live-work, rental
  housing, that is affordable to extremely low-, very low-, low-, or
  moderate-income households, including necessary operating
  subsidies.

  2. Allocate, upon State approval, $334,526 of the Year 3 Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation toward eligible activity #1, and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contacts (and any other
  required documents) with Los Angeles County Development Authority for
  the 5-year Permanent Local Housing Allocation Plan grant period and for
  Year 3 of the allocation and make adjustments as necessary to reflect the
  actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

  J. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 23-38 APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24
  SENATE BILL 1 ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT PROJECT LIST

  Senate Bill 1, also known as the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017,
  provides the City of San Gabriel with access to funds for basic road
  maintenance, rehabilitation, and safety projects. In Fiscal Year 2023-24, the City
  will receive an estimated $975,535. To qualify for funding under the Act, the
  City must adopt a list of eligible street improvement projects. The Resolution
  presented for Council’s consideration would adopt the project list and
  authorize the Public Works Director to file the required documents with the
  California Transportation Commission to receive the funding.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-38 and
  authorize the Public Works Director to file the necessary documentation to
  satisfy SB1 funding requirements and act as the authorized signatory for
  matters related to this year’s funding.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  7
  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NOS. 689 AND 690 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO INCLUSIONARY HOUSING AND
  DENSITY BONUS (ZTA23-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  On March 2, 2023, information and options related to a potential code update
  and amendment to introduce an inclusionary housing requirement and update
  to the existing density bonus ordinance were presented to the Planning
  Commission and City Council in a joint study session to provide comments.
  Following discussions, the Planning Commission recommended approval to the
  City Council of the proposed zone text amendments Ordinance No. 689 and
  Ordinance No. 690. The proposed Zone Text Amendment would amend
  Chapter 153 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to Inclusionary
  Housing and Density bonus. The Fiscal Year 2022-23 Adopted Budget includes
  the cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by
  the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing, discuss proposed Ordinance No. 689 and
  Ordinance No. 690;

  2. Motion to waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 689 and
  Ordinance No. 690 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL.
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO INCLUSIONARY HOUSING
  AND DENSITY BONUS.

  3. Motion to waive further reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second
  reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council
  meeting. The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after
  adoption.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 20, 2023  8

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
